assessments.reasoning: The pinned json/details/AFL-2.0.json records AFL-2.0, Academic Free License v2.0 and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Its crossRef and seeAlso both identify the 20060924134533 archive of www.opensource.org/licenses/afl-2.0.txt, marked non-live in crossRef.
The unsigned annotated tag v3.29.0 in spdx/license-list-data names commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48 as its object target. That commit appears in the URL for AFL-2.0.json.
OSI’s archived afl-2.0.php identifies v2.0 in the heading and notice and labels afl-2.0.txt “Plain Text Version.” The link connects the two publication routes at the edition level.

In the July 17, 2003 license-discuss message, Rosen explicitly submits Academic Free License version 2.0 for review and points to rosenlaw.com/afl2.0.html. His comparison to OSL2.0 identifies a separate instrument and describes reciprocity as a difference.

challenge.method: Compared the tag target with the detail revision, checked its single reference against the OSI HTML’s plain-text link, and examined the submission for possible confusion with OSL 2.0 or an approval decision.
challenge.results: The same edition-specific filename appears on both routes, and the HTML notice agrees with the SPDX header. The submission explicitly requests a future decision and distinguishes AFL from reciprocal OSL. These observations support documentary correspondence only.

limitations: The cited September plaintext snapshot and the inspected April HTML snapshot are distinct. The plaintext bytes and the submitted draft’s equality to the published legal body were unverified.
Rosen’s statements about combining software and his request for approval do not establish blanket compatibility or the board’s eventual decision.
reasoning: SPDX’s tagged detail assigns AFL-2.0 to Academic Free License v2.0. The inspected OSI HTML gives the same edition and explicitly links afl-2.0.txt as its plain-text version. Rosen’s dated submission independently identifies the name he submitted.
